summary: David P. Chandler studied at Harvard College, Harvard University, Yale, and the University of Michigan. A scholar in history, archaeology, and other fields, he held posts at Monash University (~1972–1997), Johns Hopkins (~1993–1994), Cornell, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

David P. Jackson is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Southampton, the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg, and under several Rinpoches. He served as a C-3 professor at the University of Hamburg (1992–2007).

David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa (attested 1993), and also studied under Lobsang Tenzin and Geshe Thubten Tandhar.

David Phillip Stanley, working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano. He served as associate professor at Naropa University and co-director of the Nitartha Institute (attested 2019).

David Pingree specialized in Indology and history/archaeology. Educated at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Otto E. Neugebauer, he held posts at Chicago (1963–1971), Brown University as department head (1971), and Cornell as Professor-at-Large (1981–1986, 1995).

David R. Kinsley specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Drew University, Union Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1965–1970). He spent his career at McMaster University (1969–2000), serving as department chair.

David R. Loy works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Carleton College, King's College London, Hawaiʻi, and the National University of Singapore (PhD ~1980–1984), he held posts at Singapore (1978–1984), Bunkyo University (1990–2006), and Xavier University (~2006–2010).

David Ralph Quinter, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology, earned an MA from Colorado and a PhD from Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure. He held posts at Indiana, Washington University in St. Louis, and Alberta (professor from 2008).
David Reigle works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and held a post at Asian Humanities Press (attested 2006).

David Roy Shackleton Bailey was a scholar in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cambridge (BA, MA, Litt.D.), he held positions at Cambridge (1944–1968), the University of Michigan (1968–1974, 1988–2002), and Harvard University (1975–1988).
David Ruddell was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Laval University and held a post as Secretary at Fort William College.

David Schaberg is a sinologist who studied at Stanford University and earned his PhD in Comparative Literature at Harvard (~1990–1996). Since 1996, he has held posts at UCLA, serving as dean of Humanities in 2012 and professor in 2020.

David Seyfort Ruegg was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the EPHE (~1951–1957). He held chairs and professorships at Leiden University (1966–1972), the University of Hamburg (1983–1990), and SOAS University of London (~1992–1996).

David Shea worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at Trinity College Dublin (1793–1798) and served as Assistant Professor at the East India Company College (1826–1836).

David Slakter works in Indology and philosophy. He earned a master's degree from the University of Liverpool under Christopher Bartley (2007–2012) and became an assistant professor at Camden County College in 2024.
David Steindl-Rast is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna and the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna between ~1945 and 1952.

David Teplitz was an Indology scholar who earned an M.A. at Northwestern University and a Ph.D. at the American Academy of Asian Studies. He held a teaching post at the California Institute of Integral Studies.

David Tracy worked in religious studies and philosophy. Educated at St. Joseph's Seminary and the Pontifical Gregorian University, he taught at the Catholic University of America (1967–1969) before serving as a distinguished professor at the University of Chicago (1969–2006).

David W. Chappell worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Mount Allison, McGill, and Yale (Ph.D. ~1968–1976), he served as professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1971–2000) and taught at Soka University of America (2000).

David W. Tien is a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He studied at McGill University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Michigan, where he earned his PhD under the supervision of James Robson (attested 2009).
